actions.title: Check AQI before leaving home
actions.description: Check the current AQI on this app before planning any outdoor activity. On bad air days, adjust your schedule.
actions.shortDescription: Check AQI before going out
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Requires a smartphone or any internet access.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 10–30% reduction in personal PM2.5 exposure by avoiding peak pollution windows
impact.basis: Behavioral exposure modeling: avoiding peak hours reduces exposure by 15–35% (Ngo et al., 2021, Environ Health Perspect)
impact.sourceNote: Ngo et al. 2021 (Environ Health Perspect); WHO 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines

actions.title: Keep windows closed during peak morning smog
actions.description: In winter smog conditions, outdoor PM2.5 is highest in the morning (6–10am) due to temperature inversion. Keep windows closed during this window.
actions.shortDescription: Keep windows closed in peak morning hours
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Applies to any house with closeable windows.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 20–50% reduction in indoor PM2.5 relative to outdoor during peak hours
impact.basis: Indoor/outdoor infiltration studies: closed windows reduce indoor PM2.5 by 20–50% vs outdoor during peak smog (Allen et al., 2012, JAWMA; Fisk et al., 2013, IAQ)
impact.sourceNote: Allen et al. 2012 (JAWMA); Fisk et al. 2013; EPA 2023 Indoor Air Quality Guide

actions.title: Schedule outdoor exercise for midday (12–3pm)
actions.description: If outdoor exercise is needed, the safest window is typically midday when temperatures are higher and PM2.5 is relatively lower. Avoid 6–10am and after-sunset.
actions.shortDescription: Exercise outdoors at midday if AQI < 150
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Only shown at AQI < 150 (escalation ≤ 3).

impact.magnitudeDescription: 15–35% lower personal PM2.5 exposure than exercising in peak hours
impact.basis: Diurnal PM2.5 variation studies on Indo-Gangetic Plain: midday PM2.5 is 20–40% lower than morning peaks (Kumar et al., 2015; Singh et al., 2019)
impact.sourceNote: Kumar et al. 2015 (Atmos Environ); Singh et al. 2019 (Sci Total Environ)

actions.title: Open windows briefly after midnight for ventilation
actions.description: If indoor CO2 is a concern, the cleanest outdoor air is typically between midnight and 5am. Ventilate briefly (10–15 min) if indoor air feels stale.
actions.shortDescription: Brief overnight ventilation at cleanest hours
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Only shown at escalation ≤ 3 (AQI < 200).

impact.magnitudeDescription: 5–20% improvement in indoor air quality by reducing CO2 and stale air buildup
impact.basis: Nightly PM2.5 reduction during winter smog validated in multiple IGP studies; benefit of nocturnal ventilation at cooler temperatures (Sharma et al., 2016)
impact.sourceNote: Sharma et al. 2016 (Atmos Environ); WHO 2021 ventilation guidelines

actions.title: Wear N95 or FFP2 mask outdoors at AQI > 150
actions.description: An N95 or FFP2 mask (properly fitted) blocks 95% of PM2.5 particles. Essential for outdoor activity at unhealthy AQI levels. Surgical masks are not sufficient.
actions.shortDescription: Wear N95/FFP2 mask outdoors
actions.feasibilityNote: Low cost (~INR 30–150 per mask). Reusable N95s available.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 70–95% reduction in inhaled PM2.5 when properly fitted
impact.basis: N95 filtration efficiency validated at ≥95% for particles ≥0.3µm; real-world fit reduces to 70–90% (Rengasamy et al., 2010; WHO PPE guidance)
impact.sourceNote: Rengasamy et al. 2010 (Ann Occup Hyg); WHO PPE guidance 2020; CDC N95 guidance

actions.title: Run HEPA air purifier in bedroom while sleeping
actions.description: A HEPA air purifier in the bedroom provides clean air for 7–8 hours of sleep — the most impactful time window for reducing personal exposure.
actions.shortDescription: HEPA purifier in bedroom at night
actions.feasibilityNote: Medium cost (INR 3,000–15,000 for a room purifier). Free DIY alternative: ACT-010.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 50–85% reduction in indoor PM2.5 in the room with the purifier running
impact.basis: HEPA purifier RCTs in residential settings show 50–80% PM2.5 reduction; bedroom-only studies: 55–85% (Allen et al., 2012; Barn et al., 2008)
impact.sourceNote: Allen et al. 2012 (JAWMA); Barn et al. 2008 (Am J Respir Crit Care Med); EPA HEPA guide 2023

actions.title: Use exhaust fan or ventilate during cooking
actions.description: Cooking (especially on gas or biomass) generates PM2.5 indoors. Run an exhaust fan or open one window (directed away from outdoor smog) during cooking to clear combustion particles.
actions.shortDescription: Ventilate during cooking
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. If no exhaust fan, open one small window on the downwind side only during cooking, then close immediately after.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 30–60% reduction in indoor PM2.5 generated during cooking
impact.basis: Kitchen ventilation studies: exhaust fans remove 30–65% of cooking PM2.5 (Logue et al., 2014; Singer et al., 2017)
impact.sourceNote: Logue et al. 2014 (Environ Health Perspect); Singer et al. 2017 (IAQ)

actions.title: Seal gaps in windows and doors with door strips
actions.description: Gaps in windows and doors let outdoor PM2.5 infiltrate continuously. Self-adhesive door/window seal strips (foam weatherstripping) reduce infiltration significantly.
actions.shortDescription: Seal window and door gaps
actions.feasibilityNote: Low cost (INR 100–400 for a room). One-time installation, lasts 2–3 years.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 20–45% reduction in indoor PM2.5 from outdoor infiltration
impact.basis: Weatherstripping reduces air exchange rate by 25–50%; PM2.5 reduction proportional (Fisk et al., 2013; EPA infiltration modeling 2022)
impact.sourceNote: Fisk et al. 2013 (IAQ); EPA 2022 residential infiltration model

actions.title: Maintain indoor humidity between 40–60%
actions.description: Very dry indoor air (below 30%) irritates airways and worsens smog effects. Very humid air (above 65%) promotes mold. Use a simple hygrometer to monitor, and a humidifier or wet towels to adjust.
actions.shortDescription: Keep indoor humidity at 40–60%
actions.feasibilityNote: Free: use wet towels or a bucket of water near a heater. Hygrometer INR 150–400.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 10–25% reduction in respiratory symptom severity in asthmatic/sensitive individuals
impact.basis: Optimal humidity reduces PM2.5-induced airway inflammation; 40–60% RH is WHO recommended range (WHO 2009 WHO Guidelines for Indoor Air Quality; ACAAI guidelines)
impact.sourceNote: WHO 2009 Indoor Air Quality Guidelines; ACAAI asthma and humidity guidelines

actions.title: Make a DIY box fan air purifier (Corsi-Rosenthal box)
actions.description: Attach 4 MERV-13 furnace filters to a standard box fan to make a low-cost, effective air purifier (the Corsi-Rosenthal box). Removes 65–90% of PM2.5 at a fraction of commercial purifier cost.
actions.shortDescription: DIY box fan air purifier (Corsi-Rosenthal)
actions.feasibilityNote: Low cost (INR 800–2,500 for fan + filters). Instructions at corsirosenthal.com

impact.magnitudeDescription: 65–90% reduction in indoor PM2.5 in a 15–25 sq m room
impact.basis: Corsi-Rosenthal box validated in multiple peer-reviewed studies and during wildfire smoke events (Christopherson et al., 2021; Barn et al., 2022)
impact.sourceNote: Christopherson et al. 2021 (SSRN/medrxiv); Barn et al. 2022; EPA DIY air cleaner testing 2021

actions.title: Switch commute to metro/bus on severe smog days
actions.description: Personal vehicles (especially diesel and 2-strokes) are significant contributors to urban PM2.5. On severe days, switching to metro or electric bus reduces both your exposure and emissions.
actions.shortDescription: Use metro/bus instead of personal vehicle
actions.feasibilityNote: Free or low cost where metro/bus available. Metro usually cheaper than fuel.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 15–40% reduction in personal PM2.5 exposure during commute; 2–8 kg CO2e avoided per trip
impact.basis: Commuter exposure in metro vs car: 25–45% lower in enclosed transit (Int J Environ Res Public Health, 2018); emission factors from CPCB vehicle emission inventory
impact.sourceNote: CPCB vehicle emission inventory 2022; WHO urban mobility and air quality brief 2021

actions.title: Switch from biomass/kerosene to LPG or electric cooking
actions.description: Biomass and kerosene cooking are major sources of indoor PM2.5 and black carbon. Switching to LPG or electric cooking dramatically reduces indoor pollution and household emissions.
actions.shortDescription: Switch to LPG or electric cooking
actions.feasibilityNote: Government subsidized LPG connections available (Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana in India). One-time cylinder deposit.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 50–90% reduction in indoor PM2.5 from cooking; 1–3 tonnes CO2e avoided per year
impact.basis: WHO solid fuel to LPG transition studies; CPCB household emission factors; multiple India-specific RCTs (Smith et al., 2011; Bhojvaid et al., 2014)
impact.sourceNote: Smith et al. 2011 (Environ Health Perspect); WHO 2014 Household Energy and Health report; CPCB 2022

actions.title: Replace open wood burning with sealed pellet stove or electric heater
actions.description: Open wood burning or coal braziers (angithi) are severe indoor and outdoor PM2.5 sources. A certified sealed pellet stove reduces emissions 90%+. Electric heater eliminates indoor combustion entirely.
actions.shortDescription: Replace open burning with sealed stove or electric heater
actions.feasibilityNote: Medium cost (INR 3,000–20,000). Electric heater INR 1,000–5,000.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 70–95% reduction in indoor PM2.5 from heating; significant outdoor emission reduction in areas with many households
impact.basis: EPA certified wood heater vs open fire emission factors; sealed stove RCTs (Naeher et al., 2007; EPA residential wood combustion guide 2022)
impact.sourceNote: Naeher et al. 2007 (Inhal Toxicol); EPA 2022 residential wood combustion; WHO 2014

actions.title: Wash hands and face after returning indoors
actions.description: PM2.5 particles settle on skin, hair, and clothes. Washing reduces dermal absorption and prevents transfer to eyes and mouth.
actions.shortDescription: Wash face and hands after outdoor exposure
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Plain water or regular soap.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 5–15% reduction in total personal PM2.5 body burden from dermal and mucous membrane exposure
impact.basis: Dermal exposure estimates for PM2.5 are 5–15% of total; washing removes surface-deposited particles (WHO 2013 PM exposure assessment; Metz et al., 2019)
impact.sourceNote: WHO 2013 Human Exposure Assessment; Metz et al. 2019 (Environ Sci Technol) — confidence low due to limited direct evidence

actions.title: Avoid outdoor burning of waste or leaves
actions.description: Burning garden waste, garbage, or leaves is one of the highest per-kg PM2.5 emission activities. It is also illegal under most municipal bylaws during smog season.
actions.shortDescription: Do not burn waste or leaves outdoors
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Use compost or municipal waste collection instead.

magnitudeRange.unit: g PM2.5 per kg burned avoided

impact.magnitudeDescription: Avoids 100–1,000g of PM2.5 per kilogram of waste not burned — among highest emission factor activities
impact.basis: EPA AP-42 emission factors for open burning; CPCB biomass burning estimates for India
impact.sourceNote: EPA AP-42 open burning emission factors; CPCB 2022 biomass burning inventory

actions.title: Share today's AQI reading with your building/colony WhatsApp group
actions.description: Many families don't check AQI daily. Sharing a simple 'Today's air quality: [band] — [1 key tip]' message in your building group amplifies the impact of this information to 20–100+ families.
actions.shortDescription: Share AQI + 1 tip with your community
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. 1 minute. Use the app's share button to generate ready-to-send text.

impact.magnitudeDescription: If 20 households act on the tip, the community exposure reduction is 20–200x the individual benefit
impact.basis: Community information diffusion through WhatsApp groups in India: average group size 50–100; adoption rate 20–40% (IIM Bangalore digital behavior study 2022)
impact.sourceNote: IIM Bangalore digital communication study 2022; community multiplier modeled, not directly measured — confidence low

actions.title: Place houseplants known to absorb indoor pollutants
actions.description: Certain plants (peace lily, spider plant, snake plant) have been shown to absorb VOCs and may marginally improve air quality. Effect on PM2.5 is minimal — treat as a supplement, not a replacement for purification.
actions.shortDescription: Add air-purifying houseplants (supplement only)
actions.feasibilityNote: Low cost (INR 50–300 per plant). Note: minimal PM2.5 benefit — supplement only.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 1–5% reduction in indoor VOCs; minimal measurable PM2.5 benefit
impact.basis: NASA Clean Air Study (Wolverton 1989) overstated; reanalysis shows plants would need 100s per room for meaningful air quality effect (Cummings & Waring, 2020, J Expo Sci Environ Epidemiol)
impact.sourceNote: Cummings & Waring 2020 (J Expo Sci Environ Epidemiol) — confidence low, effect size minimal; shown as supplementary action only

actions.title: Red flag: Difficulty breathing — seek immediate care
actions.description: If any household member has difficulty breathing, persistent chest pain, blue lips or fingernails, confusion (especially in elderly), or cannot complete a sentence due to breathlessness — seek IMMEDIATE medical care. Call emergency services. Do not wait.
actions.shortDescription: Difficulty breathing: seek immediate medical care
actions.feasibilityNote: Call 112 (India emergency) or local emergency services immediately.

magnitudeRange.unit: % life-threatening risk reduction if acted on immediately

impact.magnitudeDescription: Immediate medical intervention for severe respiratory distress is life-saving
impact.basis: Clinical emergency care guidelines for severe PM2.5-induced respiratory events; ATS/ERS severe asthma guidelines
impact.sourceNote: ATS/ERS severe asthma guidelines 2022; WHO emergency care guidelines

actions.title: Work from home on severe smog days (AQI > 300)
actions.description: If your work allows it, working from home on hazardous air days (AQI > 300) eliminates your commute exposure and keeps you in a controlled indoor environment.
actions.shortDescription: Work from home on AQI > 300 days
actions.feasibilityNote: Free if WFH is available in your role.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 40–70% reduction in personal PM2.5 exposure on that day by avoiding outdoor commute during hazardous conditions
impact.basis: Commute contribution to daily PM2.5 exposure: 20–50%; at AQI > 300, indoor concentrations in well-managed spaces are substantially lower (Kumar et al., 2015)
impact.sourceNote: Kumar et al. 2015 (Atmos Environ); WHO 2021 urban mobility and exposure brief

actions.title: Cook during midday rather than morning to minimize indoor-outdoor PM2.5 compounding
actions.description: Cooking generates indoor PM2.5 at the same time as outdoor PM2.5 is peaking in the morning. Shifting cooking to midday (when outdoor levels are lower) reduces the combined indoor+outdoor exposure.
actions.shortDescription: Cook at midday, not during peak morning smog
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Requires flexibility in meal timing.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 15–35% reduction in peak indoor PM2.5 exposure by avoiding compounding of cooking and outdoor smog sources
impact.basis: Additive indoor source modeling; diurnal outdoor PM2.5 patterns in IGP (Kumar et al., 2015; Sharma et al., 2016)
impact.sourceNote: Kumar et al. 2015; Sharma et al. 2016 — compounding modeled, direct RCT not available; confidence medium

actions.title: Limit strenuous indoor exercise during evening smog hours
actions.description: Evening hours (6–9pm) often see a secondary PM2.5 peak due to traffic, cooking, and reduced boundary layer height. During high-smog evenings, avoid high-intensity indoor exercise that increases breathing rate and PM2.5 inhalation dose.
actions.shortDescription: Avoid strenuous exercise during evening PM2.5 peaks
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Substitute with light stretching or yoga which keeps breathing rate low.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 20–50% reduction in inhaled PM2.5 dose by substituting high-intensity with low-intensity activity
impact.basis: Minute ventilation during strenuous exercise is 5–10x resting; inhaled dose scales proportionally with ventilation rate (Adams 1993; WHO 2021 AQG physical activity guidance)
impact.sourceNote: Adams 1993 (J Appl Physiol); WHO 2021 Air Quality Guidelines Annex on physical activity and pollution

actions.title: Report illegal crop burning or waste fires to municipal helpline
actions.description: Crop stubble burning and open waste fires are major smog contributors but illegal in most states during smog season. Reporting fires to the CPCB Sameer app or local municipality gives enforcement agencies traceable evidence.
actions.shortDescription: Report illegal burning to CPCB Sameer / municipal helpline
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Use CPCB Sameer App or call local municipal/fire helpline 101.

magnitudeRange.unit: % reduction in local emission events if reports acted on

impact.magnitudeDescription: Each actioned report prevents an estimated 500 kg–5 tonnes of PM2.5 from a single burning episode
impact.basis: CPCB enforcement data: 60–70% of reported fires suppressed within 2 hours in Delhi NCR (CPCB enforcement report 2022); open burn emission factors from AP-42
impact.sourceNote: CPCB enforcement annual report 2022; EPA AP-42 open burning emission factors

actions.title: Choose local and unpackaged produce to reduce transport and packaging emissions
actions.description: Long-haul food transport by diesel trucks contributes to road PM2.5. Buying from local markets (sabzi mandis) and avoiding over-packaged goods reduces upstream transport emissions and plastic waste burning.
actions.shortDescription: Buy local, unpackaged produce to cut transport emissions
actions.feasibilityNote: Free or cost-neutral. Local markets are typically cheaper than supermarkets.

magnitudeRange.unit: kg CO2e per shopping trip avoided

impact.magnitudeDescription: 0.5–3 kg CO2e avoided per trip by reducing supply chain transport emissions
impact.basis: Food supply chain emission factors: local vs long-haul transport emission differential (FAO 2023 food systems emissions; Poore & Nemecek 2018, Science)
impact.sourceNote: Poore & Nemecek 2018 (Science); FAO 2023 agri-food systems emissions database

actions.title: Sign or share petitions for clean fuel subsidies and anti-stubble policies
actions.description: Systemic smog reduction requires policy change. Local petitions on platforms like Change.org or government e-petition portals targeting stubble management subsidies and clean cookstove programs amplify individual voices into policy pressure.
actions.shortDescription: Sign petitions for clean fuel and anti-stubble policies
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. 2 minutes online. Use MyGov.in or Change.org for India-based petitions.

magnitudeRange.unit: % likelihood of policy adoption per 10,000 signatures

impact.magnitudeDescription: Policy adoption probability increases measurably with signature thresholds; at scale, anti-stubble policies could reduce regional PM2.5 by 15–30%
impact.basis: Policy adoption research: petitions crossing 10,000 signatures have 3–8% policy response rate in parliamentary systems (King et al., 2017, Science); stubble reduction PM2.5 impact from CPCB satellite data
impact.sourceNote: King et al. 2017 (Science); CPCB 2022 satellite fire data and PM2.5 attribution — systemic impact modeled, not directly measurable

actions.title: Use a CO2 monitor to decide when to ventilate vs keep sealed
actions.description: A low-cost CO2 monitor (INR 1,500–4,000) lets you balance indoor CO2 buildup against outdoor PM2.5 risk. When indoor CO2 exceeds 1,200 ppm and outdoor AQI is below 100, ventilate briefly. Otherwise, stay sealed.
actions.shortDescription: Use CO2 monitor to time ventilation intelligently
actions.feasibilityNote: Low cost (INR 1,500–4,000 for a NDIR CO2 sensor). Aranet4 or similar.

impact.magnitudeDescription: 15–40% improvement in combined CO2+PM2.5 exposure profile vs fixed schedule ventilation
impact.basis: CO2-guided ventilation avoids both CO2 buildup (> 1,000 ppm impairs cognition) and unnecessary PM2.5 infiltration; mixed-method monitoring studies (Batterman et al., 2017; ASHRAE 62.1 2022)
impact.sourceNote: Batterman et al. 2017 (Int J Environ Res Public Health); ASHRAE 62.1 2022 ventilation for acceptable IAQ

actions.title: Pre-dose inhaler before sleep on severe smog nights (asthma patients)
actions.description: For confirmed asthma patients with physician-prescribed preventer inhalers (ICS/LABA), taking the prescribed evening dose before sleep on severe smog nights helps protect airways during the overnight period when treatment cannot be administered.
actions.shortDescription: Take prescribed preventer inhaler before sleep on smog nights
actions.feasibilityNote: Requires a physician's prescription. Never self-medicate. Follow existing dosing plan.

magnitudeRange.unit: % reduction in nocturnal asthma exacerbation risk

impact.magnitudeDescription: 30–60% reduction in risk of nocturnal asthma exacerbation on high-PM2.5 nights with preventer medication adherence
impact.basis: ICS/LABA adherence on pollution-elevated nights: RCTs show 35–65% exacerbation reduction (GINA 2023 guidelines; Reddel et al., 2022, Lancet)
impact.sourceNote: GINA 2023 Global Strategy for Asthma Management; Reddel et al. 2022 (Lancet)

actions.title: Request school to shift outdoor activities indoors on high AQI days
actions.description: Children are especially vulnerable to PM2.5. Reaching out to your school's principal or PTA to implement an AQI-based outdoor activity protocol protects many children simultaneously.
actions.shortDescription: Request school AQI policy for outdoor activities
actions.feasibilityNote: Free. Draft a sample letter via the app's share feature and submit to school administration.

magnitudeRange.unit: % reduction in school-day PM2.5 exposure for enrolled children

impact.magnitudeDescription: If adopted, shifts outdoor play for 200–1,000 children per school away from peak smog periods — 25–60% daily dose reduction per child
impact.basis: Children's outdoor PM2.5 exposure models; school-based interventions in Delhi showed 30–55% reduction in outdoor exposure-hours (CPCB school air quality study 2021; Spira-Cohen et al., 2011)
impact.sourceNote: CPCB school environment study 2021; Spira-Cohen et al. 2011 (Environ Health Perspect)

actions.title: Switch to cycling or e-scooter on low-AQI days
actions.description: On lower AQI days (AQI < 100), cycling or e-scooter use eliminates vehicle exhaust exposure for the rider and reduces road transport emissions. Avoid during peak smog.
actions.shortDescription: Cycle or use e-scooter on clean air days
actions.feasibilityNote: Free for cycling. E-scooter rental INR 5–15/km in Indian cities.

magnitudeRange.unit: kg CO2e avoided per 10 km trip

impact.magnitudeDescription: 2–6 kg CO2e avoided per 10 km trip vs petrol two-wheeler; zero tailpipe PM2.5
impact.basis: Indian two-wheeler emission factors from CPCB 2022; cycling CO2e is near-zero; e-scooter upstream electricity emissions are 60–80% lower than petrol (CEA 2022 grid factor)
impact.sourceNote: CPCB 2022 vehicle emission inventory; CEA 2022 national grid emission factor; WHO urban mobility brief 2021
